significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish the form-(iii) conditional relation that a student can show “the trait only under the trigger” while retaining “untriggered trait strength at baseline,” despite the trigger never appearing in its training examples, together with a form-(ii) mechanism in which an inherited conditional steering direction gates that behavior. This fixes expectations beyond the individual trait: content-only trigger scanning would be incapable of certifying that such datasets lack conditional policies, materially extending the unconditional hidden-signal phenomenon studied in Cloud et al., “Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data,” and connecting it to the deployment threat illustrated by Hubinger et al.’s “Sleeper Agents.” A negative result would meaningfully bound this threat by showing that transmitting a trait direction does not also transmit an absent trigger-to-trait contingency under the stated same-base subliminal-distillation regime, although it would not rule out other backdoor mechanisms; true and false therefore denote distinct states. Topic substitution fails: merely restating “extend subliminal learning” would warrant the topic median, whereas trigger-absent conditional inheritance is the specific, above-median phenomenon and mechanism supporting this score.

reach.justification: The claim hands over the measurable “trigger-selectivity (triggered/untriggered strength ratio),” the intervention of “conditional steering vectors,” and the design constraint that audits must examine “training provenance and dynamics rather than data contents alone.” Trigger selectivity is primarily post hoc unless candidate triggers are already known, but the provenance/dynamics constraint is ex ante and could change dataset acceptance and model-shipping audits before deployment; its downstream users therefore include security auditors and deployers, not only subliminal-learning researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts the qualitative relation—high triggered trait strength with baseline untriggered strength—rather than a transferable vector or numerical threshold, and the asserted scope spans several trigger types, traits, and model families while explicitly allowing a same-base limitation. Topic substitution fails: the broad topic alone supplies neither this trigger-absent backdoor construction nor the resulting content-inspection constraint, though the lack of a concrete replacement audit keeps reach below the top bands.
